business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Asset On-Chain Tax Calculation and Bookkeeping SaaS

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2023 Revision), ss.4(1), 5, 6(1) and 8(1) (exempted company incorporation); and, where applicable, Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (as amended), overseas company registration provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Grand Cayman; secondary registration with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, if operating from a Gibraltar office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (responsible for corporate income tax self-assessment and issuance of Tax Reference Numbers); corporate registry filings are made with the Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar. Official portal: www.gibraltar.gov.gi (Government of Gibraltar / Income Tax Office online services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman Exempted Company establishing a branch or place of business in Gibraltar must: (1) register as an Overseas Company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies within one month of establishing a place of business under the Companies Act 2014, filing certified Cayman incorporation documents, constitutional documents, register of directors/members, and a Gibraltar registered office address; (2) upon Companies House registration, the Registrar automatically notifies the Income Tax Office, which issues a Tax Reference Number (TRN); (3) file a self-assessment tax return each year of assessment (YA runs 1 July to 30 June) based on accounts for the accounting period ending in the preceding calendar year. No minimum capital requirement applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope - The Cayman Exempted Company remains wholly exempt from direct taxation in the Cayman Islands under the Companies Act (Cayman), while its Gibraltar branch is chargeable to Gibraltar income tax on a territorial basis only: Gibraltar-source trading profits are taxed at 12.5%, foreign-source income is excluded, and no tax is levied on capital gains, dividends, interest, or royalties where sourced outside Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections under the Income Tax Act 2010 include: (1) election for Gross Income-Based Assessment (GIBA) applicable to regulated financial services businesses (e.g., insurance, banking, trust companies) at reduced gross-basis rates instead of profit-based assessment; (2) election for the qualifying Intellectual Property (Patent Box) regime for eligible software/crypto-tax-IP royalties, subject to economic substance and nexus requirements; (3) application of hybrid mismatch rules under Gibraltar's Income Tax (Amendment) legislation aligning with OECD/EU ATAD principles, disallowing mismatched deductions otherwise arising from the Cayman/Gibraltar parent-branch structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None - Gibraltar levies no VAT, GST, or sales and use tax. Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area and the UK VAT regime (20%) does not extend to the territory. Limited customs/excise duties apply only to imports of physical goods such as alcohol, tobacco, fuel, and personal effects.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A - No turnover-based indirect tax registration threshold exists in Gibraltar because no VAT/GST/sales tax system is in force. A physical import of goods may attract excise/import duty per the Gibraltar Customs tariff schedule, but no registration threshold applies to the delivery of digital SaaS services or cryptocurrency payment rails.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing, API reporting, or digital stamping regime exists in Gibraltar. The Income Tax Office accepts standard electronic invoices and accounting records; taxpayers must retain supporting documentation for at least six years. Commercial e-invoicing and blockchain-based transaction records are permitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in the traditional VAT sense, as no VAT is imposed in Gibraltar. The equivalent export-favourable outcome is the territorial sourcing exclusion under the Income Tax Act 2010: revenue earned by the Cayman Exempted Company's Gibraltar branch from the supply of digital on-chain tax calculation and bookkeeping SaaS services to non-resident customers is treated as foreign-source income and excluded from Gibraltar chargeable income, provided the contracts are negotiated and executed outside Gibraltar, the services are performed in part or wholly outside the territory, and the branch maintains demonstrable economic substance in Gibraltar. No formal zero-rating application is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - required only for physical exports of tangible goods from Gibraltar; not required for cross-border digital SaaS or software-as-a-service delivery

Bill of Lading / airway bill - physical exports only; for digital services, substitute blockchain transaction confirmation / delivery logs evidencing remote provision of the crypto-tax software platform

Inward Remittance Certificate - bank statement or SWIFT credit confirmation from a Gibraltar-licensed bank evidencing receipt of fees from non-resident customers, together with supporting SaaS licensing agreement and invoices
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner of Income Tax may reopen assessments within 6 years for negligent or incorrect returns and up to 21 years where fraud or wilful default is established. Penalties under the Income Tax Act 2010 include: up to 100% of the tax undercharged for incorrect/negligent returns; up to 200% of the tax undercharged for fraudulent returns; daily default penalties of GIP 10; and interest at 8% per annum on unpaid tax. If the foreign-source income exclusion is claimed but the branch lacks economic substance or artificially routes revenue through the Cayman Exempted Company to avoid Gibraltar tax, the Income Tax Office may reverse the exclusion, re-characterise the full amount as Gibraltar-source income, impose the 12.5% corporation tax, and apply penalty and interest retroactively.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority for GBP and the pegged Gibraltar pound, GIP) and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) (banking, payment services and DLT regulatory supervisor; Gibraltar has no separate central bank and no exchange-control authority).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The GIP is pegged at 1:1 to GBP and is freely convertible; sterling is legal tender in Gibraltar. Both current account and capital account transactions are effectively free of exchange-control restrictions following the repeal of UK exchange controls in 1979. A Cayman Exempted Company may therefore invoice, settle, repatriate profits and remit dividends in any convertible currency without obtaining prior central-bank approval. The practical hurdles are not regulatory approvals but rather bank/EMI KYC acceptance, source-of-funds substantiation, and Gibraltar economic-substance obligations if the company is centrally managed and controlled in Gibraltar.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline requiring export receipts to be converted into GIP/GBP. Export/sales proceeds may be retained in the original invoice currency, including USD, EUR, GBP, and USDC where the receiving institution maintains compliant stablecoin or crypto-asset custody/settlement rails. For SaaS/crypto tax-accounting receivables, the company should document underlying licence agreements and invoice references to preserve a clean audit trail.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Escrow and Settlement Account / Private Banking Mandate
Capital Escrow and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-High for payments-only fintech/EMI services such as Stripe, Wise or UK-licensed EMIs where the Cayman Exempted Company can evidence genuine software/SaaS activity and no client-money custody. However, post-Brexit UK/EEA EMI licences are not automatically passportable into Gibraltar; a GFSC-recognised e-money/payment institution or a Gibraltar DLT-licensed entity is required for regulated stablecoin payment services. The crypto tax-accounting app itself does not require a statutory banking licence, nor does processing only its own SaaS revenue create a payments-firm trigger, but any future custody of customer tokens or client money would broaden the GFSC authorisation perimeter.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally possible under GFSC AML/CFT guidance for low-risk corporate structures, but Gibraltar banks commonly require at least a video interview combined with certified/legalised corporate documents; in practice, physical attendance by at least one director or the compliance officer in Gibraltar or London substantially increases account approval probability. The Cayman registered agent must provide a certificate of good standing, registers, incumbency and letter of non-tax-residence; all beneficial owners should expect to provide biometric ID, source of wealth and source of funds documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Exempted Company with no audited financial statements, no physical office and no granted economic substance in Gibraltar
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide orphan/agent structure chart, Cayman certificate of incorporation, good standing certificate, registered agent incumbency letter, articles of association, share register, beneficial ownership declaration, management/audited accounts, business plan, client contracts, and a written premise that management and substance remain in the Cayman Islands/UK/Gibraltar as applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-asset / digital ledger business activity flagged as high AML risk by bank compliance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the GFSC DLT/Travel Rule risk assessment, AML/CTF policies and procedures, token-screening logic on the tax-accounting SaaS platform, evidence that the firm does not custody client assets or execute unlicensed payment processing, proof of voluntary GFSC DLT registration (if any), external audit report on blockchain analytics, and regulated-bank references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or key principal domiciled in a high-risk or heightened-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compile source of wealth statement, source of funds trail, certified passport and proof of residential address, tax residence certificate, professional reference from a regulated legal/accounting firm, explanation of corporate commercial purpose, and clearing exchange/wallet forensic report for any crypto-derived beneficial-owner proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan injections from the Cayman parent/beneficial owners into the Gibraltar operating account should be routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes denoting equity capital contribution (e.g. P0101 general commercial payment / P1105 intra-group financing) and must be supported by an executed board resolution and share/loan documentation. SaaS subscription receipts may arrive via Stripe, USDC, or direct SWIFT/Ach; USDC collections should be converted through a GFSC/UK FCA-compliant exchange under a two-account structure (hot wallet with withdrawal whitelists and cold treasury storage), then settled in GBP/EUR/USD to the bank account with a matching invoice reference. Every inbound transfer should include the LEI-embedded legal entity name and the specific subscription/customer reference for reconciliation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for cloud infrastructure, licensing, legal, payroll and software tools should be executed by SWIFT MT103 straight-through processing in the supplier's own currency, or by card and local payment rails (SEPA, Faster Payments/Chaps) where the Gibraltar bank provides coverage. Commercial letters of credit (sight LC or usance LC) are permissible but generally only appropriate for physical-goods transactions; for this software tax-accounting SaaS, seller-hosted recurring payments and smart-contract USDC disbursements are preferred. A controlled zero-balance treasury should be used, with same-day sweeps from operating account to a regulated deposit/MMF account, and all outbound crypto disbursements must pass through a GFSC-compliant travel-rule and sanctions screening engine.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts in GBP/USD and GBP/EUR with a GFSC-regulated or UK FCA-authorised bank, limited to underlying contractual fx exposure.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in GBP/USD where the counterparty bank accepts a GBP reference rate; NDFs directly on GIP are generally unavailable due to the hard parity peg to GBP.
Cross-currency swaps between USD and GBP/EUR for balance-sheet hedging of long-term crypto-denominated receivables and debt instruments.
Vanilla European-style FX options (call/put) for hedging subscription revenue or procurement costs in USD/EUR/GBP.
Zero-cost FX collars and tunelling structures for medium-term treasury risk management when traded with a licensed Gibraltar/UK bank under ISDA documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Annual Return and Annual Government Fee (exempted-company renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January for each registration year running 1 July to 30 June; companies incorporated after 1 July pay a pro-rated fee at incorporation and resume the 31 January cycle in the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing surcharge on the annual fee (capped at CI$500) accruing after 31 January; if unpaid for five months through 30 June, the Registrar may administratively strike off and dissolve the company; restoration requires a court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Register of Directors Return and Annual Data Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation submitted with the Annual Return by 31 January; any change in directors or particulars must be filed within 60 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Officers personally liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding CI$500 (approx. US$610) plus a CI$50 daily default fine; information is reconciled against the Beneficial Ownership Register held at the registered office

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return (Companies Act 2014, Form A) and Up-to-Date Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days following each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed late-filing penalty of GIP£250, escalating default fines up to GIP£5,000 on prosecution, inability to obtain an Up-to-Date Certificate for banking and transactional purposes, and risk of administrative strike-off for chronic non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First accounts within 15 months of incorporation; annually thereafter within 9 months of the accounting reference period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating penalty: GIP£50 (up to 3 months late), GIP£250 (4-6 months), GIP£500 (7-12 months), GIP£1,000 (over 12 months); directors may be publicly named and prosecuted for persistent failure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Corporate Income Tax Return (including crypto-asset turnover and token-balance disclosures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (proXes online portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 November for the year of assessment ending the previous 30 June (e.g., Y/A 2025 covering 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025 is due 30 November 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Best-of-judgment assessment by the Commissioner, default penalties up to 100% of under-assessed tax, monthly late-filing fines, statutory interest on unpaid tax, and criminal fines up to GIP£10,000 for negligent or fraudulent returns

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (Central Beneficial Ownership Database)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary; material changes in beneficial ownership filed within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers liable on summary conviction to fines up to GIP£5,000 and/or up to 6 months' imprisonment plus a daily default fine of GIP£100; non-compliant companies are blocked from statutory transactions and filings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Gibraltar: statutory audit is compulsory for public-interest entities, large companies, and any company failing two of the three small-company tests (annual turnover not exceeding GIP£10.2 million, balance-sheet assets not exceeding GIP£5.1 million, average employees not exceeding 50); a shareholder holding at least 10% of issued shares may also demand an audit. Cayman: no statutory audit applies to a standard exempted company outside regulated activities (funds, banking, insurance) and outside the Economic Substance relevant-activity regime; audits are typically imposed by shareholder agreement or lender/banking covenants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Gibraltar statutory accounts follow IFRS as adopted in the EU/Gibraltar; Cayman exempted companies may present financial statements under IFRS or US GAAP. For the crypto-tax SaaS model, digital-asset holdings are measured under IAS 38 (own-use intangibles), IAS 2 (tokens held for sale) or IFRS 9 (financial instruments/fiats), with revenue from token-based subscriptions recognised under IFRS 15.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Gibraltar requires a central-filed Beneficial Ownership Register with annual confirmation within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary and event-driven updates within 30 days; Cayman requires the Beneficial Ownership Register to be maintained at the registered office and confirmed annually to the registered agent by 31 January (not publicly searchable). Share transfers in both jurisdictions must be posted to the Register of Members within 30 days, and the Gibraltar side requires a refreshed Up-to-Date Certificate for the new capitalisation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) with transfer history and share-capital annotations
Register of Directors (and Register of Secretaries where one is appointed)
Minute Book of board and general meetings, Register of Charges, and option/warrant registers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500-US$3,000 per annum for a licensed Gibraltar corporate services provider covering the registered office, registered agent, secretarial administration and statutory filings; retained Cayman registered-agent services add US$1,200-US$2,000 per annum where the Cayman-incorporated vehicle is kept
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,500-US$12,500 per annum for a small-company IFRS audit by a Gibraltar accounting firm; US$1,800-US$3,500 per annum for an audit-exempt reporting accountant's compilation or agreed-upon-procedures report
